pdf-a-word.title: PDF to Word
pdf-a-word.description: Turn your PDF into editable Word text without the file ever leaving your device.
pdf-a-word.cta: Need to digitize documents at scale for your company? Let's talk about a custom solution.
pdf-a-word.seoTitle: PDF to Word Converter, Free and Private | SonhoLab
pdf-a-word.seoDescription: Convert PDF to Word free in your browser: your file never leaves your device. No signup, no watermark and no limit on how many files you convert.
pdf-a-word.intro: A lot of PDFs arrive locked: you can't fix a date, a price or a paragraph without rebuilding the whole thing from scratch. This tool pulls the text out of the PDF and hands you a Word document you can actually edit, and it does all of that inside your browser, without uploading the file anywhere.
pdf-a-word.stepsHeading: How to convert your PDF to Word
pdf-a-word.step1Text: Drag the file onto the box or click to browse your computer. The PDF opens in your browser and never travels to a server.
pdf-a-word.step2Text: It starts with the text already in the document. If the PDF is a scan, it runs optical recognition page by page, which takes a bit longer.
pdf-a-word.step3Text: When it finishes, you download the Word file and open it in Word, Google Docs or LibreOffice to edit, copy or forward it.
pdf-a-word.useCase1: A quote comes in as a PDF and you need to change prices and dates before sending it back to the client.
pdf-a-word.useCase2: You have a scanned contract and need to copy two clauses without typing them out again by hand.
pdf-a-word.useCase3: You're writing a university paper and want to quote paragraphs from an article that only exists as a PDF.
pdf-a-word.faq1q: Do my files get uploaded to a server?
pdf-a-word.faq1a: No. The conversion happens inside your browser, on your own device. The PDF is never sent to SonhoLab or to anyone else, no copy is stored anywhere and nobody else can open it. That's why it works for contracts, invoices or documents with personal data.
pdf-a-word.faq2q: Is it free? Is there a limit on files?
pdf-a-word.faq2a: It's free and there's no account to create. You can convert as many PDFs as you want, with no queue and no watermark on the result. Since the work runs on your own machine, the only real limit is your device's memory with very heavy files.
pdf-a-word.faq3q: Do I need to install any software?
pdf-a-word.faq3a: No. It runs in the browser you already have, on a computer or a phone, and there's no extension to add. Only the first conversion of a scanned PDF downloads the text recognition model, which is then ready for the ones after it.
pdf-a-word.faq4q: Does it work with scanned PDFs or photos of documents?
pdf-a-word.faq4a: Yes. When it sees that a page has almost no text, it switches to optical character recognition. That first run takes longer because it downloads the model. The result depends on the scan: if it's crooked or blurry, you'll have errors to fix.
pdf-a-word.faq5q: Will the Word file look exactly like the PDF?
pdf-a-word.faq5a: Not exactly. The tool recovers the text so you can edit it, not the layout: complex tables, columns and images can end up somewhere else. If you need the formatting as it was, go through the document and fix those parts before you send it.
